# The habit: the run, the receipt and a moment

How many weeks in a row a person has been on time, with one late week forgiven; what the check-in’s last screen says once the week’s are all in; and when a check-in says a goal reached its target or came back on track.

## The rule

The habit Faro most wants is checking in before the review without being asked. This page is the part a person sees about themselves; nothing here compares people, and a run is only ever shown to its owner.

**The run** (`onTimeStreak`). A week is *on time* when the person had something due in it and every goal they own that was due was checked in by them on or before the week's review day (the end of the day: reviews have a day and no hour). Walk back from the latest finished week (this week counts once every goal is checked in; otherwise start from last week), counting on-time weeks. A week that is not on time is **forgiven** when each of the 4 weeks before it in which the person had something due was on time: it isn't counted, and the walk goes on. A week not on time and not forgiven ends the walk, and so does a week with nothing due. "Checked in this week, but late" is a late week like any other. `forgivenIn` gives the latest forgiven week inside the run, or none. The forgiving run is the default (CF4); a workspace setting to make it strict or hide it comes with CF2's `streak` column, which isn't built: until then every workspace forgives.

**The receipt** (`receiptText`, from `receiptFacts`), once every one of the person's check-ins for the week is in. It reads their goals this week, how many of them were first checked in after the due day, and the deadline in dueWords' words (`dueWords` with `heldOnDueDay` for the person: "before {Thursday}’s review" only while Reviews is on and a live review they are in is held that day; otherwise "by {Thursday}", and Faro never calls a deadline a review), the run, the forgiven week and the next due day:

- all in by the due day: "{Your check-in is | Both of your check-ins are | All {n} of your check-ins are} in before {Thursday}’s review." (in no review held that day, or with Reviews off, "… in by {Thursday}.": the deadline is dueWords', [rule RS1](../../modules/reviews/rules.md)), then, from a run of 2, "That is {k} weeks in a row."; and on the first receipt after a forgiven week (it is last week), "Week {w} came in late; one late week doesn’t break a run.";
- some after: "{…} in. {It | One | Both | All of them | {m}} came after {Thursday}’s review." (or "came after {Thursday}.") then "The next {is | are} due by {Thursday 19 Nov}." No run is mentioned, and none is said to be lost.

Never said: "streak lost", "broken", a nought, a count of late weeks, an exclamation mark. A person is never told that an ask came before their check-in. Home's quiet line says the same two sentences on the day the week is completed ([Home](home.md)), and `get_my_work` gives them as `weekReceipt`.

**A moment** (`moment`, for the goal's earlier check-ins and this one). *Reached*: a number goal's value meets its target in the goal's direction (at or above it when the target is above the start, at or below it otherwise) and the latest check-in of the week before did not. *Back*: the status is On track, the week before's was At risk or Off track, and the goal had been behind (At risk or Off track) for 2 weeks or more in a row. Reached wins over back; one per check-in. Neither fires on a correction, a second check-in in the same week, a backfilled week or an import. The receipt shows one panel above the week's lines: the status's shape and word (Done, or On track), "{Goal} reached its target" and "{value}, against a target of {target}, in week {w} of {weeks}. It started the year at {start}." with **Copy the share image** and **See the goal**; or "{Goal} is back on track" and "{value}, after {k} weeks behind plan." with **See the goal**. History's row for that check-in adds "Reached its target" or "Back on track" in small capitals, in the status's colour, with no capsule. `post_check_in` answers with the same `moment`. No animation beyond the receipt's own, no confetti, no banner on anyone else's screen.


## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Tunde (one goal, due Thursday) at week 46, on time: weeks 41–46 with 45 late; 41–46 with 44 and 45 late; 44–46 with 45 late (nothing due before 44); 36–46 with 40 and 45 late. | `5, week 45 forgiven / 1 / 1 / 9, week 45 forgiven` |
| Two check-ins in by Thursday, a run of 5, week 45 forgiven. | `Both of your check-ins are in before Thursday’s review. That is 5 weeks in a row. Week 45 came in late; one late week doesn’t break a run.` |
| Four check-ins, one after Thursday’s review, a run of 5. | `All 4 of your check-ins are in. One came after Thursday’s review. The next are due by Thursday 19 Nov.` |
| One check-in, by someone in no review held on Thursday; then one after the deadline. | `Your check-in is in by Thursday. / Your check-in is in. It came after Thursday. The next is due by Thursday 19 Nov.` |
| Deploy lead time (40 h → 20 h): 22 h in week 45, then 20 h in week 46; then 28 h on track after 34 h At risk and 35 h Off track. | `Deploy lead time reached its target: 20 h, against a target of 20 h, in week 46 of 53. It started the year at 40 h. / Deploy lead time is back on track: 28 h, after 2 weeks behind plan.` |
| The same 20 h, backfilled. | `none` |

- [src/domain/review.ts](../../../src/domain/review.ts): `heldOnDueDay`

## Requirements

- `HABIT-RECEIPT`: Once a person's check-ins for the week are all in, the receipt says whether they were in before the deadline ("All 4 of your check-ins are in for week 46, before Thursday’s deadline."; the due day is called a review only for someone in a review held that day) and the run of weeks in a row on time, from two; or how many came in after it and when the next are due, with no run. One late week is forgiven when the four weeks before it were on time, and said once ("Week 45 came in late; one late week doesn’t break a run."). Never "lost", "broken", a nought or an exclamation mark. Home's quiet line says the same two sentences on the day the week is completed.
- `HABIT-MOMENT`: A check-in that reaches a goal's target, or brings it back on track after two weeks or more behind, shows one quiet panel on its receipt (the status's shape and word, what happened in one line, "Copy the share image" for a target reached) and its row in the goal's History says "Reached its target" or "Back on track" in small capitals. Never on a correction, a backfilled week or an import; no animation, confetti or banner on anyone else's screen.

- the forgiving run (CF4, built unconditionally until CF2 adds cycle.streak) › counts every week when all are on time
- the forgiving run (CF4, built unconditionally until CF2 adds cycle.streak) › treats this week, checked in late, as a late week like any other
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › says every check-in is in before the review, and the run from two weeks
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › says a forgiven week once, on the first receipt after it
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › says how many came after, the next due day, and no run
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › says the deadline, not a review, to someone in no review that day (deep review T4), in dueWords’ words
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › with Reviews off, says “by Thursday” and “after Thursday” even where a review is held (Reviews switch spec 2.1)
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › with Reviews on, names the review as in spec 2.1
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › never says a run was lost or broken
- the receipt (spec 2.1) › reads its facts from the week (receiptFacts)
- the moment (rule 3) › is reached when the value meets the target and the week before did not
- the moment (rule 3) › is back when on track after two weeks or more behind
- the moment (rule 3) › reached wins over back
- the moment (rule 3) › never fires on a backfilled week or a correction
- the moment (rule 3) › is said in the receipt’s words
